Technical and design decisions:
1. Use Spring Boot profiles to enable automatic, context-aware selection of the Admin SPI implementation (Receptor, CloudController, or local) based on deployment environment, removing the need for manual configuration switches.
2. Implement a common base ModuleRegistry abstraction prior to building concrete SPI implementations to ensure consistent behavior, reduce code duplication, and simplify future SPI extensions.
3. Utilize Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka as the service registry and metadata store for module discovery and metadata persistence, leveraging existing project investments in the Spring Cloud ecosystem.
4. Store custom module names and full module metadata in Eureka's native metadata map to support name-based search and rich module information retrieval without modifying Eureka's core data model or requiring additional infrastructure.
5. Host all Admin SPI implementations in a dedicated shared Maven/Gradle module to provide a single, versioned, reusable location for contributors to access and extend the SPI codebase.
6. Reuse existing Spring XD core domain classes (ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus) across all SPI implementations to maintain consistency with the broader Spring XD codebase and avoid redundant domain modeling.

Assumptions:
1. Existing Spring XD core infrastructure (including ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus classes, base module deployment logic, and test harnesses) is already available and does not require new development.
2. A production-ready Eureka server instance is already deployed and accessible for Spring Cloud Services (s-c-s) use cases, with no need to provision or configure Eureka server infrastructure as part of this increment.
3. Stable, well-documented client libraries for Receptor and Cloud Foundry Cloud Controller are available as project dependencies, so low-level API client implementation is not required.
4. The target runtime environment is compatible with Spring Boot 3.x and Spring Framework 6.0+, as specified in the provided project documentation.
5. No changes to existing Spring XD module deployment logic are required beyond the new self-registration and metadata publishing features described in the user stories.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot's profile mechanism to enable automatic selection of the appropriate Admin SPI implementation based on deployment context, eliminating manual configuration requirements.
Define a common base ModuleRegistry abstraction before implementing concrete SPI implementations to ensure consistent behavior, reduce code duplication, and simplify future SPI extensions.
Leverage Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka as the service registry and metadata store for module discovery and metadata persistence, aligning with the existing Spring Cloud ecosystem used by the project.
Store custom module names and full module metadata in Eureka's native metadata map to support name-based search and rich module information retrieval without modifying Eureka's core data model.
Host all Admin SPI implementations in a dedicated shared Maven/Gradle module to provide a single, versioned, reusable location for contributors to access and extend the SPI codebase.

Reuse existing Spring XD core domain classes (ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus) across all SPI implementations to maintain consistency with the broader Spring XD codebase and avoid redundant domain modeling.
assumptions: Existing Spring XD core infrastructure (including ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus classes, base module deployment logic, and test harnesses) is already available and does not require new development.

A production-ready Eureka server instance is already deployed and accessible for Spring Cloud Services (s-c-s) use cases, with no need to provision or configure Eureka server infrastructure as part of this increment.
Stable, well-documented client libraries for Receptor and Cloud Foundry Cloud Controller are available as project dependencies, so low-level API client implementation is not required.
The target runtime environment is compatible with Spring Boot 3.x and Spring Framework 6.0+, as specified in the provided project documentation.
No changes to existing Spring XD module deployment logic are required beyond the new self-registration and metadata publishing features described in the user stories.

activities.activity_name: Design and implement core module registry abstraction
activities.activity_description: Define the base ModuleRegistry interface and abstract implementation that encapsulates common module management logic (registration, status tracking, listing) to serve as the foundation for all Admin SPI implementations, including comprehensive unit tests for the abstraction.

Build the concrete Admin SPI implementation that integrates with the Receptor control plane to implement getStatus(), listModules(), and getAllStatuses() APIs, using the core module registry abstraction, with unit and integration tests for all functionality.

Build the concrete Admin SPI implementation that integrates with the Cloud Foundry Cloud Controller API to implement the three Admin SPI methods, using the core module registry abstraction, with unit and integration tests for all functionality.

Set up a dedicated shared Maven/Gradle module in the project's common repository, configure build and dependency management, and add contributor documentation for using and extending the SPI implementations.

Configure Spring Boot profiles and conditional bean loading to automatically select the correct Admin SPI implementation based on deployment context (local jar, Cloud Foundry push, LTC create), including profile-specific configuration properties and validation.

Add logic to Spring XD modules to automatically register with Eureka on installation, including publishing module metadata, health status, and handling registration lifecycle events (startup, shutdown, failure).

activities.activity_name: Implement name-based module search in Eureka
activities.activity_description: Extend Eureka integration to store custom module names in Eureka's metadata map and add query logic to filter and search modules by their custom name, in addition to the default spring.application.name, with corresponding unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement module metadata storage in Eureka
activities.activity_description: Define the module metadata schema, implement storage of full module metadata (version, configuration, dependencies) in Eureka's metadata map, and add retrieval logic to expose this metadata via the Admin SPI, with unit and integration tests.
Write user documentation for deploying and using the profile-aware Admin service, and update contributor guides to cover the new SPI implementations and module registry abstraction.

activities.activity_name: End-to-end integration testing and defect resolution
activities.activity_description: Execute end-to-end tests to validate all user story requirements, including profile switching, SPI functionality, Eureka integration, module search, and cross-component compatibility, and fix any identified defects.
